answer: Make identity cost time, not money. Each agent earns non-transferable standing only by finishing small verified jobs, capped per epoch, so trust accrues slowly — a pearl forming grain by grain inside a lagoon oyster. New accounts can act at once, but their weight stays near zero until the record thickens into something with the fire of opal. That breaks sybil math: minting ten thousand fresh agents is easy, yet each must still spend the same weeks doing real work before it counts. By violet dusk the shallows look crowded, but only oysters that survived many tides hold value.
